messages:
claire: Heads-up: runtime + control-plane alignment needed for claim lifecycle. We keep having ambiguous behavior around renew jitter, eviction semantics, and what information to surface to SDKs. Quick sync to capture a decision.
dan: TL;DR proposals: (1) canonical lease states: ACTIVE, DRAINING, FORCED; (2) claim token payload must pin model id+sha and mode; (3) eviction events include cache_action and origin.
priya: small nit: name DRAINING vs DRAIN - prefer DRAINING to indicate active process. Also propose default TTLs baked into modes: hosted=90s, dedicated=30s, private=300s. Runtimes attempt renew at TTL/3 with +/-10% jitter.
ben: agree on states. For wave-off behavior: DRAINING should reject new sessions with 429 + Retry-After header; keep streams alive up to drain_timeout. FORCED immediately terminate streams with final event {"type":"lease_forced","reason":"PREEMPT"}.
claire: how do we report reason machine-readably? Plan: header X-RW-Lease-State, X-RW-Lease-Reason (CAPACITY, AUTHZ, RESTART), X-RW-Cache-Action (invalidate|preserve|async). And a final stream JSON event for streaming responses.
dan: token semantics: JWT with claims: sub, mode, pin (model@sha), allowed_fallbacks[], iss (control-plane or delegated issuer), exp. Private runtimes can accept delegated tokens if issuer verifies via configured root cert. No wildcards in pin.
priya: private edge-case: control plane can't reach runtime behind NAT. Runtime must persist lease journal to local storage (/var/lib/redwood/lease-journal) and expose /_internal/lease/journal for eventual postback. On reconnect it POSTs entries to control plane.
ben: caching: if eviction reason=AUTHZ or COMPROMISE -> immediate synchronous cache invalidation. If PREEMPT -> async_invalidate; runtime returns job_id and control plane polls /_internal/cache/job/{id}. Avoid blocking eviction on slow cache invalidation.
claire: metrics & alerts: lease_renew_latency_ms, lease_renew_failures_total{reason,mode}, lease_evictions_total{reason,mode}. Alert if renew_fail_rate > 0.5% p5 across region.
dan: eviction selection when capacity tight: sort by (sla_score asc, tenant_weight asc, connection_age desc). Allow billing overrides via tenant.eviction_weight tag. Keep deterministic tie-breaker: runtime_id hash.
priya: SDK ergonomics: on 429 from new sessions during DRAINING, SDK should wait Retry-After then try a different runtime or fallback route. For streams if final lease event is received, SDK should surface a LeaseError with structured fields (state, reason, cache_action).
ben: rollout: probe-first behavior in hosted/dedicated (control plane queries /_internal/capabilities and manifests). For private use optimistic-run but mark runtime manifest stale when not reachable; require operator opt-in to enable risky features.
infra-bot: ci: lease-protocol branch pushed, canary deploy scheduled.
claire: decision notes: I'll draft RFC with these defaults and headers. Action items: @dan write token format snippet; @priya document journal postback shape; @ben add cache job API sketch; add SDK update checklist.
dan: will sketch JWT claim example and sample header shapes today.
priya: I'll add playbook entry for NAT reconnect scenarios.
ben: will add cache job schema and CLI: `rwctl lease inspect --runtime RT-123`
claire: thanks all — creating RFC PR and tagging reviewers. :rocket:
